lessonRef.focus: two-way frequency tables, joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: two-way frequency tables, joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: For ŷ = 4x + 60, interpret the slope where x is hours studied.

steps: Slope is change in y per unit x.
One more hour is associated with about 4 more points.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: Ice cream sales and swimming-pool admissions are strongly positively correlated across a year. What conclusion is justified?
choices: Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.
Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.

items.prompt: A data set records 29, 3, 14, 23, 3, 40, 34. Give the mean and the median.
choices: mean 23, median 20.86
mean 20.86, median 23
mean 20.86, median 21
mean 21, median 23

items.prompt: A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 203 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.
Both the mean and the median rise sharply.
Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.
The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 49 yes, 5 no; row 2: 24 yes, 59 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 11x + 18, where x is measured in hour studieds and y in test points. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional hour studied is associated with an increase of about 11 test points.
The predicted value is 11 test points when x is 0.
Each additional test points is associated with 11 more hour studieds.
Each additional hour studied causes an increase of exactly 11 test points.

items.prompt: Towns with more fire engines report more fire damage. What conclusion is justified?
choices: Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.
Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: A data set records 4, 30, 3, 14, 9, 26, 34. Give the mean and the median.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
